Recruiting

### Canine Osteosarcoma Vaccine Trial

● University of Queensland, School of Veterinary Science

Experimental vaccine trial for dogs recently diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma. Two vaccine formulations being assessed. Dogs must be proceeding to surgery with no evidence of metastasis. All breeds eligible.

Cancer All dogs QLD

📅Open now  ·  🐾Ongoing enrolment

### Feline Diabetes Treatment and Monitoring Studies

● University of Queensland, School of Veterinary Science

Three concurrent studies for diabetic cats and cats in diabetic remission. Two studies investigate exenatide (Bydureon), a long-acting synthetic drug. A third evaluates continuous glucose monitors that provide readings without needles. No cost to owners for diagnostics, study drugs, or monitoring.

📅Open now  ·  🐾Diabetic cats needed

View source →UQ Vet School

### Canine Osteoarthritis Pain Management Study

● University of Sydney, Veterinary Teaching Hospital

Evaluating a novel anti-inflammatory compound for management of chronic osteoarthritis pain in dogs aged 5 years and older. Multi-site, placebo-controlled study design.

📅Expected Q3 2026  ·  🐾60 dogs needed

### Canine Cognitive Decline and Gut Microbiome Study

● University of Melbourne, Veterinary School

Longitudinal observational study examining the relationship between gut microbiome composition and cognitive function in ageing dogs. Involves stool collection and cognitive assessments over 12 months.

📅Expected Q2 2026  ·  🐾100 dogs needed

### Antimicrobial Prescribing in Companion Animal UTI

● University of Melbourne, Asia-Pacific Centre for Animal Health

Prospective intervention study examining antimicrobial prescribing behaviour for urinary tract disease in dogs and cats. Evaluating the impact of free culture and susceptibility testing and decision support tools on antibiotic use in general practice clinics across metropolitan Melbourne.

📅Active 2024-2026  ·  🐾21 clinics enrolled

● Murdoch University, The Animal Hospital

Clinical research into immunotherapeutic approaches for solid tumours in companion animals. Led by the oncology service at The Animal Hospital at Murdoch University, with particular focus on novel checkpoint inhibitor combinations.

# Clinical trial for dogs with splenic haemangiosarcoma

  * Dr Sonya Yu
  * Clinical Research
  * Oncology

### Has your dog recently undergone spleen removal for haemangiosarcoma? Join our clinical trial combining immunotherapy with chemotherapy.

MediPaws is participating in a multi-centre clinical trial, led by the University of Melbourne, investigating a novel treatment approach for dogs with splenic haemangiosarcoma. This study evaluates the use of an autologous tumour vaccine (a personalised vaccine made from your dog’s own tumour) in combination with standard chemotherapy (doxorubicin).

This research has been reviewed and approved by the University of Melbourne Animal Ethics Committee (Project ID 35274).

# Why participate?

### Helping advance treatment for haemangiosarcoma

This study is exploring whether stimulating the immune system alongside chemotherapy can improve outcomes for dogs with this aggressive cancer.

### Meaningful benefits for your dog

Dogs enrolled in the study will receive:

  * Standard-of-care chemotherapy with a veterinary oncologist
  * Access to a personalised tumour vaccine at no cost
  * Close monitoring by a specialist oncology team
  * Contribution to research that may improve future treatment options

### Eligibility

Dogs may be eligible if they:

  * Have a confirmed diagnosis of splenic haemangiosarcoma
  * Have undergone splenectomy (surgical removal of the spleen)
  * Have no visible evidence of metastatic disease prior to starting chemotherapy
  * Are planned to receive doxorubicin chemotherapy

Eligibility is confirmed by Dr Sonya Yu,  the MediPaws oncologist.

# What’s involved?

### What happens in the study?

Your dog will receive standard chemotherapy as planned. The study adds a personalised vaccine created from the original tumour tissue.

Treatment and monitoring are performed alongside routine oncology care.

### Participation requirements

There are no major additional procedures beyond standard treatment and follow-up.

Participation is voluntary, and you may withdraw at any time.

# Costs

The autologous vaccine is provided free of charge.

Standard veterinary care, including chemotherapy and associated costs, are not covered by the study.

# Interested in enrolling?

MediPaws is actively enrolling dogs into this clinical trial.

If you think your dog may be eligible, we recommend contacting MediPaws directly or speaking with your veterinarian to discuss suitability and next steps.

Our oncology team can guide you through eligibility, treatment planning, and enrolment.

# Register your interest in our dog cancer trial

We are recruiting dogs with mast cell cancer in Australia for an investigational trial of personalised mRNA cancer vaccines. Register your interest and share a few details about your dog. Our team will contact you about further screening.

Why we are running this trial

## From Rosie’s story to a future for more dogs.

Image: Rosie

Rosie

The first dog treated with a personalised neoantigen vaccine.

It began with Rosie. Her experience with a personalised neoantigen vaccine encouraged Paul to explore how this approach could one day be made available to every dog with cancer.

Before an approach like this can become broadly available, we must study it carefully and support it by evidence for review by the relevant veterinary regulators. This clinical trial is an important step in that process, helping us learn from participating dogs and understand the vaccine more fully.

Read Rosie’s personalised mRNA cancer-vaccine story  →

Who can register

## If your dog has cancer and is currently in Australia, you’re welcome to register your interest. Our team will check whether your dog may be eligible for this trial.

Register your interest  →

About the trial

## What this trial is looking at

The trial will investigate a personalised mRNA vaccine approach for dogs with mast cell cancer. Tell us about your dog and our team will help determine whether they may be eligible for screening.

Image

### Who can register

Dogs diagnosed with mast cell cancer who are based in, or able to travel within, Australia.

Every case is reviewed individually

Image

### The trial approach

A therapeutic mRNA vaccine designed from each dog’s own tumour and blood samples, intended to work alongside—not replace—existing care.

Personalised to each dog

Image

### What screening involves

We help coordinate records, screening, sample logistics and updates, working with the trial team and your treating veterinarian.

A named team stays in touch

Trial registration and screening

## How to register your interest.

You don’t need to have every record ready before registering your interest. Start with what you know and we’ll help with the rest.

01

### Register your interest

Complete a short form with basic details about your dog, their mast cell cancer diagnosis and where you live.

02

### We get in touch

A Gamgee coordinator will contact you, answer practical questions and—with your permission—help gather relevant records from your vet.

03

### The trial team confirms eligibility

The authorised study team and treating veterinarian assess potential eligibility. If your dog may proceed, you’ll receive the approved trial information and consent discussion before deciding.

These are indicative timings from a single case. Sequencing turnaround and manufacturing schedules may vary. We will give you a case-specific estimate before proceeding.

## Ready to tell us about your dog?

Registering your interest does not guarantee eligibility or enrolment. Please continue your dog's existing veterinary care while your information is reviewed.

Register your interest  →

## Veterinary Programme

  * “The Heeler Study” is a Phase 1/2 clinical trial at a leading Australian university, expected to commence in Q4 2026, continuing the evaluation of Selvax immunotherapy in dogs with naturally occurring cancers, which has previously shown encouraging results.
  * Advancing clinical-ready formulation work to support future development and clinical translation.
  * Preparing to draft the Pre-IND package to support future regulatory engagement with the FDA.

02 / Pre-Clinical

## Human Programme

  * Preparing Pre-IND documentation for the Selvax immunotherapy platform in human solid tumours, with an initial focus on pancreatic and head and neck cancers, which have proven challenging to treat with conventional immunotherapy and chemotherapy.
  * Advancing pre-clinical development through significant CMC work that builds on the programme's existing formulation and development.
